{"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-ttfo.3","title":"process_dio keeps stale parent rank on inflation, enabling rank loops","description":"## Location

python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py process_dio loop-prevention check (~224-228). After a parent is already in self.parents, a later DIO with dio.rank >= self.rank (and < INFINITE_RANK) hits return without updating or removing the candidate.

Poison (dio.rank >= INFINITE_RANK) does parents.pop plus select_parent. Rank inflation into [self.rank, INFINITE_RANK) does not.

## What goes wrong

RFC 6550 section 8.2.2.5: a node MUST NOT use a parent whose advertised Rank is greater than or equal to its own. Python compares dio.rank >= self.rank and, on match, leaves the old lower rank in the table. select_parent then keeps that neighbor as preferred parent using the stale cost.

Trigger:
1. Attacker A advertises rank 256. Victim V joins, V.rank=512, preferred_parent=A.
2. A now advertises rank 600 (or 512). Python ignores the update; cached A.rank stays 256.
3. V still advertises 512 and still routes V->A.
4. A, now at 600, hears V's DIO rank 512 < 600 and may select V as parent, forming a V->A->V rank loop.

test_poisoned_dio_removes_candidate only covers INFINITE_RANK. Self-parent is blocked only when node_address is set; this loop does not need self-parent.

Rust removes the neighbor and re-selects when dio.rank >= self.rank. After demote(), _lowest_rank is INFINITE so a finite high-rank parent can be installed (intended rejoin); an infinite-rank DIO is still dropped. The loop is the stale-rank path on an already-joined node, not demote itself.

## Fix

On dio.rank >= self.rank (finite), drop neighbor_id from parents and call select_parent(), matching the poison path and rust/lichen-rpl process_dio.
